results.title: Fix: Dangerous Code Execution Function Could Allow External Attacks in scrapy/shell.py
results.extractability_reason: titolo e corpo contengono 960 caratteri: la valutazione prosegue
results.accepted_requirement: The system shall prevent arbitrary code execution through external input.

iteration_history.candidate: The system shall prevent arbitrary code execution through external input in the shell module.

issues: The requirement names the affected source module. Removing 'in the shell module' still leaves a complete behaviour ('the system shall prevent arbitrary code execution through external input'), so the module name is implementation detail located by the scanner rather than part of the required behaviour.
The evidence establishes the behaviour only in general terms (input from outside the program must not be evaluated as code); it does not scope the guarantee to a named component of the codebase.
unsupported_claims: in the shell module (a file location reported by the scanner, not an externally observable scope of the behaviour)
revision_instructions: Remove the reference to the shell module/file: state the behaviour at the level of the system, as the evidence supports it.
Keep the obligation expressed as what must not happen when content originates from outside the program, without naming the evaluation mechanism or the remediation applied.

iteration_history.candidate: The system shall prevent arbitrary code execution through external input.

issues: The candidate applies the previous instruction: the module name has been removed and the obligation is stated at system level, matching the general terms the evidence supports (content originating outside the program must not be evaluated as code).

results.title: Fix: Unsafe XML Processing Library Could Allow Malicious Attacks in scrapy/http/request/rpc.py
results.extractability_reason: titolo e corpo contengono 852 caratteri: la valutazione prosegue
results.accepted_requirement: The system shall prevent malicious XML-RPC inputs from causing attacks.

iteration_history.candidate: The system shall process XML-RPC requests without allowing malicious XML inputs to cause denial of service or code execution attacks.

issues: The requirement names two specific attack outcomes - denial of service and code execution - that the evidence never mentions; the report states only that the XML-RPC handling was unsafe and could allow 'malicious attacks'.
Naming two distinct outcomes joined by 'or' also widens the sentence into more than one obligation, only the general form of which the evidence supports.
revision_instructions: Remove the two named attack classes: the evidence characterises the risk only in general terms and does not say which attacks the change prevents.

State the single general behaviour the evidence does establish, namely what must not happen when XML-RPC content originating from an untrusted source is processed, without naming the remediation library or module (defusedxml, xmlrpc) or the affected file.

iteration_history.candidate: The system shall prevent malicious XML-RPC inputs from causing attacks.

issues: The evidence describes a static-typing-only change: a cast to a subclass introduced solely to satisfy type checkers, with the body explicitly stating that runtime behaviour is unchanged and no new Failure instances are created.
A change observable only by reading annotations or running a type checker over the source fails the black-box test, so no required behaviour of the system can be grounded in this evidence.
The writer's stated reason matches the evidence and no grounded abstract requirement is reachable.
